subject: DPA - Clarify ephemeral cache retention & offline backup residency
messages:
From: Julia Stevens <julia.stevens@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acme.com>, legal@acme.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA retention language (ephemeral caches & offline backups)

Karthik —

Thanks for sending over the latest DPA redline. Our security team raised two points we need clarified before we can sign:

1) Ephemeral caches: section 4.2 references 'ephemeral caching' with no retention period. Can you confirm whether any model-serving caches (prefix caches, KV caches) may persist longer than a single request lifecycle? We need to understand maximum time-to-live and whether these caches are written to disk.

2) Offline backups and snapshots: section 7.1 allows for backups for disaster recovery but does not specify residency for backups taken for operational reasons (snapshots, cold backups). We require that backups containing Customer Data either reside in the same region as production or be encrypted with a customer-supplied key and have a defined deletion window.

We attached our annotated DPA. Please respond with explicit redlines or a short proposed clause. Happy to jump on a call if that's easier.

Best,
Julia
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation

Attachments: Acme_DPA_annotated.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Julia Stevens <julia.stevens@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA retention language (ephemeral caches & offline backups)

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers up front, then I’ll follow with proposed redlines:

- Ephemeral caches: the serving runtime uses in-memory KV caches by default; they are not persisted to disk in normal operation and individual cache entries are evicted based on usage/age. We do not intentionally persist per-request caches to durable storage, but some crash dumps or scheduled snapshots may include transient state in exceptional circumstances. Typical TTL for in-memory caches is under 10 minutes; long-tail entries are rare.

- Offline backups: we take scheduled snapshots for control-plane metadata and for model artifacts. Customer Data is only included in offline backups if the customer has enabled logging or diagnostic exports. By default, backups for hosted accounts are stored in the same cloud region as the primary data store. For enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private) we can pin backup residency and support customer-supplied encryption keys.

Sharing a proposed clause next (cc’ing our security/legal and product owners).

—Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

On attachments: I’ve uploaded our internal dataflow diagram (ephemeral-cache-flow.png) to the shared Drive link for context.
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: suggested redline for ephemeral cache + backup residency

Team —

Drafted a short, restriction-friendly redline below we can propose to Acme. Kept language operationally realistic and added an exception path for Dedicated/Private customers. Thoughts?

Proposed insertion (for DPA section 4.2 / 7.1):
"Redwood may use in-memory and short-lived caching mechanisms (including KV/prefix caches and runtime-only caches) to optimize inference performance. Such caches are transient, are not intended to be written to durable storage, and have a default maximum time-to-live of 600 seconds (10 minutes). Redwood will not intentionally include Customer Data in persistent backups as a result of normal caching behavior. In exceptional circumstances (system crash, forced diagnostics) transient state may be captured; Redwood will promptly notify Customer and will delete such state within 72 hours of capture unless retention is required by law or a valid legal process.

For customers on Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private deployments, Customer may request backup pinning to a specific geographic region and may provide a customer-managed encryption key (CMK). Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to ensure offline backups containing Customer Data reside in the Customer-designated region or are encrypted with the CMK. Deletion or rotation of such backups will follow the Customer’s instructions and the timelines agreed in the applicable Order Form."

I recommend we offer a short audit commitment and a one-time attestation that the default behavior is in-memory-only for hosted customers.

-Aditya
Sr. Product Manager, Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Julia Stevens <julia.stevens@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA - Clarify ephemeral cache retention & offline backup residency

Julia —

Thanks for the flag. Aditya’s language looks good as a starting point. A couple of small suggestions before we send back to Acme:

- Change the 72-hour deletion for crash-dump captures to 5 business days to allow for triage.
- Add a short sentence confirming that application-layer logs (if enabled by the customer) are treated as Customer Data and are subject to the retention terms in section 5.
- Offer a clause: "Customer may request a one-time backup residency attestation within 10 business days at no charge." That often calms procurement.

I’ll prepare the redline and attach it.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Julia Stevens <julia.stevens@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA - Clarify ephemeral cache retention & offline backup residency

Julia —

Appreciate the quick review. Attached is our proposed redline (DPA_redline_v3.pdf) and a short diagram showing where ephemeral caches live in the request path (ephemeral-cache-flow.png). Summary of changes we propose:

- Explicitly state ephemeral caches are in-memory-only in normal operations and have a default max TTL of 600 seconds.
- Include an "exceptional capture" clause with a 5 business day deletion window and notification commitment.
- Commit to backup residency options for Dedicated/Private and offer one-time attestation for Hosted within 10 business days at no charge.

If that looks acceptable, we can fold into the final DPA. If Acme prefers tighter language on TTL or wants CMK for hosted accounts, we’ll need to route to ProductOps for feasibility impact and potentially include a small surcharge in the Order Form.

Would you like to schedule a 30-minute call this afternoon to run through the redline?

Thanks,
Karthik
